prior_suggestions.start_name: Tie-in near the Western Desert Gas Complex (GASCO), Amreya industrial zone, Alexandria Governorate
prior_suggestions.end_name: Al-Amiriya (Amreya) LPG/Butane Extraction Plant, Alexandria Governorate
prior_suggestions.corridor_desc: This is a short (5km/18in) intra-industrial-zone connector, not a long-haul line from Rashid town on the coast (which is ~40km+ from Alexandria's Amreya district -- far too far for a 5km pipe). Multiple sources (Egypt Oil & Gas, attaqa.net, egyptoil-gas's separate piece on WDGC/Amreya output) place both the Western Desert Gas Complex (WDGC) and the Amreya LPG/butane recovery plant in the same Amreya/Merghem industrial area southwest of Alexandria city, and describe this 5km/18in line as the second phase of the Raven-field connection project -- the first phase (P6703, 70km/30in) already brings Raven-field gas from the coast to the WDGC; this short spur then carries gas the final 5km from that complex to the neighboring Amreya butane plant so it can run at full capacity. GEM's own StartLocation='Rashid' for this row (identical to sibling P6703) most likely reflects the project's field-of-origin naming convention rather than this specific segment's physical starting point. I could not find a source giving an exact facility gate or pipeline-map coordinate for either the WDGC or the Amreya LPG plant, so no lat/lon is given -- only the named facilities and the general Amreya/Merghem, southwest Alexandria vicinity, which is a tight, well-defended bound given the line's short length even without exact coordinates.

prior_suggestions.start_name: Denise/Karawan (DEKA project) subsea gas wells, Temsah Concession, offshore Nile Delta

Four gas sealines (9 km at 16-in and 4 km at 10-in) tie the subsea wells into Petrobel's existing 32-in sealine network via the Seth platform topside, which in turn runs onshore to the El Gamil Gas Plant near Port Said. No published source gives precise subsea well-head or Seth-platform coordinates, so the offshore end and the intermediate corridor are described only by bearing/distance from Port Said, not a fixed point -- left null rather than guessed. The onshore endpoint coordinate (31.2844, 32.2025) is for the named place 'El Gamil' (fort/airfield landmark, Port Said Governorate) as the nearest sourced fix to the gas plant, not a plant-specific survey point.

prior_suggestions.start_name: Rashid Petroleum Company tie-in point, near Edko, Beheira Governorate
prior_suggestions.end_name: Mahmoudia power station, Kafr Amlit, Mahmoudiya, Beheira Governorate
prior_suggestions.corridor_desc: Per GASCO's ESIA/RAP for this project: a 42in line runs from a Rashid Petroleum Company facility east of Edko City, south along/near the Edko-Damanhour road, crossing the coastal road, the Alexandria-Rashid railway, Bousily Drain and Edko Drain, to a National Natural Gas Network facility north of Bisintaway village (~27 km). A 30in line continues east from a valve room near Izbat Abdel Razeq/Hommosy, parallel to the Kom Al Gharaq canal, to a tie-in described as 'Dairut Power Station' (~17 km). A 16in line then runs south then east from a valve room on that line, crossing the Mahmoudia Canal, to the pressure-reduction station inside Mahmoudia power station (~7 km). All of this is within Beheira Governorate, Nile Delta -- no need to reach the unrelated town of Dairut in Assiut/Upper Egypt; 'Dairut Power Station' as named in the ESIA is almost certainly a second, more local beneficiary tie-in along the same corridor, not the distant Assiut town, but I could not independently confirm which facility that name refers to and flag it for a human to check when drawing the actual route line. Start/end coordinates given are town-center approximations for Edko and Mahmoudiya (public gazetteer values), not the exact valve/plant siting, which the ESIA describes only in words and route-figure captions (no coordinates given in the source text).
